matches.description: Watch AVS vs FC Porto highlights and goals from Primeira Liga on ReFooty: Football Highlights Hub. Match played on May 10, 2026. The pitch served as the stage for a high-intensity Primeira Liga clash, where the ambitions of both sides were tested under the watchful eyes of the supporters. With the match played on May 10, 2026, the atmosphere crackled with the promise of tactical battles and decisive individual moments. An electric first half Early exchanges were defined by a sharp tactical tug-of-war, with FC Porto looking to dictate the tempo against a resilient AVS Futebol SAD . The deadlock was broken in the 23rd minute when Roni found space to fire home with his left foot, sending the home crowd into raptures. Despite sustained pressure from the visitors as they hunted for an equalizer, the home side held firm, heading into the break with their noses in front. The equalizer and the surge Following the interval, FC Porto ramped up their offensive intensity. In the 53rd minute, a well-placed cross from Borja Sainz allowed Deniz Gul to head home the equalizer. However, the momentum shifted back almost instantly; just five minutes later, Roni restored the advantage with a stunning strike from outside the box. The decisive blow arrived in the 80th minute when Aderllan Santos rose highest to meet a Babatunde Akinsola delivery, nodding the ball into the net to cement the lead. Late drama and final whistle As the clock ticked down, FC Porto pushed forward in search of a comeback, but their efforts were severely hampered when Dominik Prpic was dismissed in the 90+2 minute after receiving his second yellow card. The AVS defense stood tall in the dying moments, securing a significant victory in this Primeira Liga encounter.

matches.description: Watch FC Porto vs Santa Clara highlights and goals from Primeira Liga on ReFooty: Football Highlights Hub. Match played on May 16, 2026. The Primeira Liga action intensified on May 16, 2026 , as FC Porto hosted Santa Clara in a match that promised tactical intrigue and high stakes. Both sides entered the pitch with plenty to play for, creating an atmosphere of anticipation for the 50,002 fans in attendance. A Cautious Opening at the Dragão From the first whistle, FC Porto looked to establish dominance through possession, utilizing the creativity of William Gomes and Rodrigo Mora . The hosts frequently targeted the box via set-pieces, with Mora swinging in multiple corners that kept the Santa Clara backline on high alert. However, the visitors stood firm, with Pedro Pacheco even forcing a defensive block following a well-placed corner from Sergio Araujo in the 17th minute. As the first half progressed, the game became a battle of attrition in the midfield. Santa Clara remained disciplined, frustrating the home side's attacking transitions and limiting clear-cut chances. Despite the territorial advantage held by the 'Dragons', the scoreboard remained untouched as both teams headed into the tunnel, setting the stage for a decisive second period. Own Goal Breaks the Deadlock The second half saw an increase in intensity as FC Porto pushed higher up the pitch. The breakthrough finally arrived in the 69th minute, albeit in unfortunate circumstances for the visitors. A defensive lapse saw Sidney Lima inadvertently turn the ball into his own net, gifting the lead to the hosts. This pivotal moment forced Santa Clara to take more risks, leading to a flurry of tactical substitutions including the introduction of Gabriel Veiga and later Bernardo Lima . In the dying embers of the match, the drama reached its peak. Santa Clara launched a desperate offensive, but Porto 's defense, led by Jakub Kiwior , remained resilient. In a show of pure commitment during stoppage time, Bernardo Lima successfully blocked a goal-bound effort from Andrey , sustaining an injury in the process. Despite the late scare and the physical toll of the encounter, FC Porto managed to carve out a narrow victory to secure all three points.
